records.description: A private development company the Province bought in 1974, through the short-lived Woodbridge Development Corporation, and owned outright from 7 June 1974. Its statements for the year ended 31 October 1974 list eight wholly owned subsidiaries. On 18 November 1976 it took the name Housing Corporation of British Columbia (an Order in Council of 9 November had authorized the Province's proxy to pass the resolution), and on 26 November two subsidiaries were renamed: W.K.P. Construction Ltd. (No. 91003) became Dunhill Development Corporation, a different company from the original Dunhill (No. 73385), and Fisher Developments Ltd. (No. 71787) became HCBC Construction Ltd. It sold Crown Lumber Limited on 1 November 1976 and wound up three other subsidiaries that year. On 29 September 1978 the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing directed that its operations be wound up; its real-estate sales subsidiary, Venture Realty Ltd., was sold effective 30 November 1978. It was in voluntary liquidation by 1985, its investment recovered and carried at $1, and was struck off in 1990. It is not the British Columbia Housing Corporation of 1976 (No. 52129), which became the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation, nor BC Housing.

records.description: The holding company through which the Province bought bus companies in 1975. Its own statements name its wholly owned subsidiaries: V I T Holdings Ltd., Thompson-Okanagan Transit Ltd. (formerly Tweed Line Tours Ltd.) and Vancouver Island Transit Ltd. (formerly McArthur Transportation Limited), at 31 March 1976, 1977 and 1978; V I T Holdings in turn held about 98 per cent of Vancouver Island Transportation Company, Vancouver Island Coach Lines, Gray Line & Empress Taxi & Sightseeing, Imperial Charter Service and British Columbia Parlour Car Tours. On 24 July 1978 V I T Holdings sold its 98.5 per cent of Vancouver Island Transportation Company to the Province, and by 31 March 1979 only Thompson-Okanagan Transit and Vancouver Island Transit remained, their buses leased from the Ministry of Municipal Affairs. The Province held its one issued share. In 1979/80 its $2.85 million of advances were cleared by a $38,815 return of assets and a $2,811,723 provision. Pacific Coach Lines Ltd. was held by the Province directly, not through it.

records.description: The government's bus company. Incorporated on 2 August 1978, it bought the assets of Vancouver Island Transportation Company Limited, which the Province had just bought from T.S. Holdings' group, and began operating on 31 August 1978; on 1 April 1979 it took over Pacific Stage Lines' assets and operating responsibilities from BC Hydro. The Province held its entire issued capital, two common shares, directly. Its $1,088,204 of advances were provided for in 1979/80. Its operations ceased on 31 March 1984 and it was being wound up. The company itself (No. 178561) was renamed 178561 B.C. Ltd. on 19 July 1990, the same week Royal Victorian Holdings Corporation (No. 362538) took the name Pacific Coach Lines Ltd. and Pacific Coach Lines (1984) Ltd. (No. 273925) became a numbered company: three different companies. No source read shows the Province holding it after 1985.

records.description: A poultry company the Province bought outright on 17 February 1975 for $4.8 million, with its subsidiaries Pacific Hatchery Ltd. and Western Feed Co. Ltd. (printed by Statistics Canada as Pacific Hatching and Western Feeds, beside a B.C. Testing Farms that Panco’s own statements never list). The company outlived its business: it sold its business and assets on 29 January 1979 for $12,076,253 (net $11,724,660), was renamed Surrey Farm Products Investments Ltd. on 14 February 1979, and on 4 May 1979 paid the Province a $14.8 million dividend; the Province's $4.8 million investment was then written down to $1. The shorter “Surrey Farm Products Ltd.” of the revenue schedules is the same company. By 1985, as British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd., it was being organized to run the Food Pacific 86 trade show, and its subsidiaries Surrey Farm Products Hatchery Ltd. (formerly Pacific Hatchery Ltd.) and Western Feed Co. Ltd. were wound up. It was struck off in 1992. The day of its second rename, to British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd., is not known: the old name is last printed at 31 March 1980 and the new one by 17 June 1985, so between those it is labelled Surrey Farm Products Investments with the rename’s window shown.
records.endedMeaning: struck off the register and dissolved as British Columbia Food Exhibitions Ltd. (No. 63265), by the Registrar of Companies’ notice; no source read shows the Province still holding it after 1985

records.description: The Crown holding company for the Province's forest-products interests from 1973. Through it the Province bought 79 per cent of Canadian Cellulose Company, Limited on 29 June 1973 and all the shares of Kootenay Forest Products Ltd. effective 1 March 1974; on 23 June 1975 it bought the last 2.5 per cent of Plateau Mills Ltd., the Province holding the other 97.5 per cent directly. It distributed those holdings to the Province as a dividend in 1977/78, and the Province transferred them to BCRIC on 9 March 1978. The British Columbia Cellulose Company Repeal Act (SBC 1983 c. 2) dissolved it when brought into force on 31 March 1986.

records.description: A potato processor the Province backed from 1973, holding 40 per cent of it in March 1977 (more than 40 per cent at one point, the Court of Appeal says). Its plant, equipment and pouch-potato technology were sold on 15 April 1977 to the newly incorporated Creston Valley Foods Ltd. for a $1.5 million debenture; the Province then bought out the other shareholders and, on 1 December 1977, sold the whole company to Standard Brands Limited. It was continued federally on 6 January 1978 and amalgamated into Standard Brands Canada Limited on 28 April 1978. Wholly provincial only for part of 1977, it stood at no year’s end, so the diagram, which shows each year at 31 December, does not draw it.
